title: Browse the Customers Table
target_audience: Beginner data analysts with no SQL experience

videos.title: Browse the Customers Table
videos.learning_objective: Learner locates and opens a table in the database browser to see its raw rows and columns before any manipulation.
videos.discovery_objective: Open the Customers table in the Browse Data tab.

exercise_artifact.description: A small online store dataset with a Customers table linked to an Orders table via customer_id, spanning multiple countries and over a year of order dates.

videos.new_capability: Open the Customers table in the Browse Data tab
videos.key_concept: Opening a table in a database browser lets you see the raw, unmodified rows and columns before any sorting or filtering is applied.
videos.running_example_usage: The learner opens the Customers table and observes its 500 rows and 6 columns (customer_id, name, email, country, signup_date, status) in the Browse Data tab.
videos.proof_numbers: Customers table contains 500 rows and 6 columns.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next, you will sort the Orders table by order_date in ascending order using the column header.

script_beats.text: By the end of this video, you'll see all 500 customer records laid out in front of you, exactly as they live in the database.
Before you sort or filter anything, you need to see the raw data first. If you skip this step, you might mistake a filtered view for the whole picture, and that's how real business mistakes happen.
Click the Browse Data tab at the top of the window.
Click Customers in the dropdown list.
Wait for the table to load.

action.description: Wait for Customers table to render

script_beats.text: The status bar at the bottom shows 500 rows, and the header row shows 6 columns: customer_id, name, email, city, state, and signup_date.

You're now looking at every one of the 500 customers in this database, across all 6 columns, with no sorting or filtering applied. Next, you'll take the Orders table and sort it by order_date in ascending order using the column header.
